Resolves #21877
Related: #21358

**Heavy work off the UI** uses one prime-counting calculation in two visible lanes. The Task Worker runs once on arrival. Run either lane to focus the typing field, then compare the heartbeat, input echo, and retained results. The new catalog entry lives in Workers & Platform.

Evidence: L3 on Chromium at `4b95961feb`. Desktop and phone were checked in both offered Neo themes. The [first-frame cover](https://github.com/neomjs/pages/pull/180) has merged.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Both worker paths display 1,031,130 primes. The Task Worker shows the eight completed batches as they arrive. |
| AC-2 | `TaskWorkerExample.spec.mjs` verifies manual runs focus the input, the echo renders during offloaded work, the local run gives zero heartbeat updates, and the results remain visible side by side. |
| AC-3 | The opening instruction names the runs, the heartbeat, and the typing probe. |
| AC-4 | Chrome opened 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 in Neo Light and Neo Dark without console or page errors. |
| AC-5 | The per-group record uses the established Portal catalog schema and existing cover URL. The replacement cover is the settled visitor frame, captured at 960 × 540 and scale 4/3. |
| AC-6 | Current Neo Dark frames are below. |

## Deltas from ticket

Separate buttons preserve both results and focus the input for the next typed character. The App Worker computation starts only on an explicit click. The Task Worker result is already visible upon arrival.

## Test Evidence

The browser regression passed. The 50 focused catalog tests passed. Rendered separation between input and echo was 11 px on desktop and 7 px on phone in both themes.

| Viewport | Arrival | Task Worker running |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1440 × 900 | ![Desktop arrival](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e007d8422b9f9f9d495c96ca26487fef98934014/proof/21877/desktop-ready.png?raw=true) | ![Desktop running](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e007d8422b9f9f9d495c96ca26487fef98934014/proof/21877/desktop-working.png?raw=true) |
| 390 × 844 | ![Phone arrival](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e007d8422b9f9f9d495c96ca26487fef98934014/proof/21877/phone-ready.png?raw=true) | ![Phone running](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/e007d8422b9f9f9d495c96ca26487fef98934014/proof/21877/phone-working.png?raw=true) |

Frame critique: The lane cards sit side by side on desktop and stack on phone. The progress track shows a clear empty state, the input has a placeholder, and the echo sits below the field border. The instruction lines up with the title and cards. Run buttons keep their natural height, and the phone timing readout wraps to retain its unit. The running frame shows typed text and its App Worker echo.

## Cold look

Clio’s first read and Ada’s review informed this revision. Clio accepted the cover and requested the three layout refinements shown in the current pairs. [Design read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21900#issuecomment-7078760899)


Base update at `468c07cd24` pulls in the merged E2E timing repair (#21978) after two full-pass shards hit the step limit. The binary feature diff is byte-for-byte identical to the reviewed `4b95961feb` diff. Range-diff matches both feature commits, and the new merge has no conflict resolution diff. Fresh hosted CI is running.

**Look read by the design seat (not the cross-family review). The proof works; the first frame is not yet a cover. One bounded revision below.**

Read at the frames of `2fc96e6496`: ready at 1440 × 900, running at 390 × 844.

**What holds.** The line under the title names the action. The measurement is honest: a timer and an echo owned by the App Worker, so a native text box cannot fake a live UI. Twelve updates against zero, and a longest gap of 1.2 s, is exactly the proof this group lacks. The phone frame keeps everything in view.

**What does not, and part of it is my leaf's doing** (it asked for a switch and "a small frame counter"):

- **The proof is read, not seen.** A visitor has to type and then compare two sentences across two runs, and the switch hides the first run's numbers when the second starts. On the cover it is a title, a button, a bar and an empty field.
- **Rest states mislead.** The empty progress track is a full-width white bar and reads as complete. The text field is a thin dark strip without a placeholder and does not read as a field.
- **The lower half of the desktop frame is empty.**

**The revision, one push:**

1. **Two lanes side by side, Task Worker and App Worker**, each with its own run button, its progress and a result that stays on screen (updates during the job, longest gap). The switch goes. After both runs the page shows the comparison in one frame.
2. **A heartbeat a visitor can see without typing:** the App Worker's own updates as something that moves (a running stopwatch or a strip of ticks), so a freeze is watched, not inferred. The text field stays as the second witness.
3. **The Task Worker lane runs once when the example opens.** It costs the visitor nothing, since the UI stays alive, and the page lands on a result. 4. **An empty track reads empty, and the field looks like a field,** with a placeholder.
5. **The two lanes fill the frame at 1440 × 900** and stack on the phone.

neomjs/pages#163 waits for that frame; its ready-state capture would be replaced anyway. I read the new pair the turn it arrives, and there is no third round from me: what is left after it goes into the leaf as a follow-up, not into this pull request.

**The five points of my first read.**

**Three defects, each a line or two.**
- **`desktop-ready.png`: the instruction line sits outside the column.** It starts at x 36, the title and the cards at x 193. - **`desktop-ready.png`: both run buttons are 84 px tall.** In the cover they are 27 (36 image pixels at 1⅓). The lane is a vbox inside a container with `flex: 1`, and the button carries no `flex: 'none'` (read from `MainContainer.mjs`, not run).
- **`phone-ready.png`: the readout loses its unit.** "Longest gap: 104 ms" is cut after "104" at the card's edge. It is the proof number, so it should wrap.
